subject: Food Science
title: Understanding Expiration Dates
description: A quick win: understand Understanding Expiration Dates.

hook.text: 'Best by,' 'sell by,' 'use by'—three different phrases, three different meanings. Most consumers can't tell them apart.

buildup.text: 'Best by' indicates peak quality—not safety. 'Sell by' is for store inventory. Only 'use by' suggests a safety deadline.

discovery.text: In the US, only infant formula has federally mandated expiration dates. All others are voluntary manufacturer estimates.

twist.text: Americans waste $29 billion worth of food annually by misunderstanding date labels. They throw away safe food by the ton.

climax.text: The EU is moving toward standardized 'use by' for safety and 'best before' for quality—simplifying the system for consumers.

punchline.text: 'Best by' is a suggestion, not a sentence. Learn the difference and waste less.

quiz.question: Which date label is legally required on all US foods?
options: None—only infant formula requires a federally mandated date
